points: Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His bedstead was a bedstead of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds, showing how tall and big this man was.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: All the region of Argob with all Bashan was called the land of giants, because the giants there were of Og's kin, of his family.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: The Reubenites and the Gadites had already received their inheritance with the half tribe of Manasseh, which Moses gave them beyond Jordan eastward: all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites and all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who remained of the remnant of the giants, for these did Moses smite and cast out.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: Joshua answered without bias: if thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, into the forest, and cut down there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee. Narrow means too small: if you are complaining that your lot is too small, then go to war and conquer more land.
